docs.title: Programming Course Template
docs.text:
A reusable documentation template for structured educational material: Java, C, C++, Python, JavaScript, Machine Learning, and more.

  • Getting Started

    Install, preview, and build this site.

  • Curriculum

    A sample course outline and chapter.

  • Code Examples

    Highlighted code in seven languages, with expected output.

  • Mathematics

    LaTeX via MathJax: inline, display, matrices, aligned equations.

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
• Light, dark, and system themes (use the toggle in the header).
  • Search, breadcrumbs, previous/next navigation.
  • Copy buttons on every code block.
  • Admonitions, tabs, tables, and diagrams.

docs.title: Authoring Guide
docs.text:
Reference pages that double as template validation:

  • Code Examples: seven languages, titles, line numbers, highlights, output.
  • Mathematics: the supported LaTeX syntax and limitations.
  • Components: admonitions, tabs, tables, diagrams.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• One # heading per page; file names in kebab-case (01-variables.md).
  • Folders have an index.md and appear in nav in mkdocs.yml.
  • Put reusable source files in examples/ and include them with --8<-- "programming/hello.py".

docs.title: Code Examples
docs.text:
Every block has a copy button (top right). Content tabs link, so choosing a language in one group selects it everywhere on the page.

JavaCC++PythonJavaScriptSQLBash Hello.java
public class Hello {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        for (int i = 1; i <= 3; i++) {
            System.out.println("Hello, " + i);
        }
    }
}
hello.c
#include <stdio.h>

int main(void) {
    for (int i = 1; i <= 3; i++) {
        printf("Hello, %d\n", i);
    }
    return 0;
}
hello.cpp
#include <iostream>

int main() {
    for (int i = 1; i <= 3; ++i) {
        std::cout << "Hello, " << i << '\n';
    }
}
hello.py
for i in range(1, 4):
    print(f"Hello, {i}")
hello.js
for (let i = 1; i <= 3; i++) {
  console.log(`Hello, ${i}`);
}
students.sql
SELECT name, AVG(score) AS average
FROM results
GROUP BY name
HAVING AVG(score) >= 60
ORDER BY average DESC;
hello.sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
for i in 1 2 3; do
  echo "Hello, $i"
done

Expected output (all but SQL):

Hello, 1
Hello, 2
Hello, 3

docs.title: Mathematics
docs.text: Math uses MathJax through pymdownx.arithmatex. Use $...$ or \(...\) for inline math and $$...$$ or \[...\] for display math.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• MathJax loads from a CDN, so math needs network access.
  • A literal dollar sign must be written \$.
  • Prefer one equation block per $$ pair; keep blank lines out of display math.
  • Each \\ line break needs an environment such as aligned or cases.

docs.title: Curriculum
docs.text:
A sample outline. Replace it with your subject's chapters.

Module Topic Level Estimated time 1 Variables and control flow Beginner 2 h 2 Functions and modules Beginner 3 h 3 Data structures Intermediate 4 h 4 Algorithms and complexity Intermediate 4 h 5 Project Advanced 6 h

Chapter layout

Each chapter follows: learning objectives, concept, syntax, example with expected output, step-by-step tutorial, common mistakes, exercises, summary.

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
By the end of this chapter you can:

  • Explain what a counting loop does.
  • Write one in several languages.
  • Relate loop cost to a summation.

docs.title: Concept
docs.text: A loop repeats a block of code. A counting loop runs once for each value of an index from a start to an end.

docs.title: Syntax and example
Cost of a loop
docs.text:
Summing the work done by a loop that runs \(n\) times with cost \(i\) at step \(i\):

\[ T(n) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} i = \frac{n(n+1)}{2} \]

docs.title: Step-by-step
docs.text:
1. Choose the start, end, and step.
  2. Write the loop header.
  3. Put the repeated work in the body.
  4. Run it and compare with the expected output.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
Off-by-one errors

range(1, 3) in Python stops at 2. Use range(1, 4) to include 3.

Why does my loop never end?

The loop variable is never updated, or the condition can never become false.

docs.title: Exercises
docs.text:
1. Print the numbers 10 down to 1.
  2. Print the sum of the first 100 integers and check it against \(\frac{n(n+1)}{2}\).

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A counting loop repeats work for each index; its total cost is often a sum.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Mermaid is vendored at docs/assets/vendor/mermaid/ (pinned version, MIT) and needs no network access.
  • Mermaid runs with its default strict security level.
  • Diagram source is plain text in the generated HTML until JavaScript renders it.

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Create a virtual environment and install dependencies.
  • Preview the site locally.
  • Build it with strict link checking.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
Windows (PowerShell)macOS / Linux 
python -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
pip install -r requirements.txt
mkdocs serve

python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
mkdocs serve

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000. Pages reload as you save.

Network access

Equations are rendered by MathJax loaded from a CDN, so a network connection is needed for math to display.

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
mkdocs build --strict

The output goes to site/. --strict turns broken links and warnings into errors.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Install, mkdocs serve to preview, mkdocs build --strict to verify.
